messages:
Sam: quick check — customers reporting different outputs between raw REST POST to /v1/generate and python sdk .generate() with what should be identical args. anyone seen this? :eyes:
Anjali: saw one ticket. dug in briefly — sdk does some param renaming + omission logic. examples below. can reproduce locally.
Anjali: code snippets:
```py
# python sdk call
client.generate(model=\"rwd-small\", max_tokens=64, stop=[\"\\n\"]) 
```
```bash
# raw REST
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwd-small","maxTokens":64,"stop":["\\n"]}'
```
Anjali: two things: python sdk sends snake_case keys but server accepts camelCase for top-level fields via tolerant parser. however for the nested `sampling`/`sampling_params` object we weren't mapping correctly so keys like `temperature` ended up nested differently. also SDK omits `stop` when user passes None which differs from sending `stop: null` vs `stop: []`.
Mike: ok — server historically accepted both `max_tokens` and `maxTokens`. we added a parser change last quarter that treats omitted `stop` as "use model default" and `stop: []` as "no stop sequences". that divergence can explain different outputs.
Sam: ahhh that lines up. so python sdk omitting stop when user passes None => server uses model default stops => different generation. any idea why SDK passed None instead of an explicit null?
Anjali: there's a serializer quirk: we drop keys with value is None to keep payload small. normally good, but for fields where API semantics differ between omitted vs explicit null/empty array it's a breaking change. also found a bug where temperature was serialized as a string in TS->JSON path for one branch, e.g. \"0.7\" instead of 0.7.
QA Bot: regression run: sdk-v1.12.3 vs rest-posts on 100 prompts -> 12% significant token diffs when stop is involved, 3% when sampling params differ. test-id: rg-2026-03-12-11.
Mike: options: 1) server-side tolerant fix: treat omitted stop same as explicit null (keep old model-default behavior) to preserve SDK behavior, or 2) change SDK to always serialize stop field (null/array) and map snake_case -> camelCase for nested objects. 3) quick compat header approach `X-SDK-Compat: legacy-stop` so server can choose behavior per client.
Anjali: I prefer SDK change + mapping. Less hacky and avoids header proliferation. I'll send a PR to make serializer include explicit keys for fields that have semantic differences. PR will: map nested sampling_params keys to camelCase, ensure numeric types stay numeric, and include `stop` as null if user passed None.
Sam: sounds good. timeline? we should coordinate API team and QA so we don't flip behavior unexpectedly for other SDKs.
Anjali: aiming for PR today, tests tomorrow. will add a feature flag so we can release toggled if needed. PR plan: add unit tests, update integration contract tests.
Mike: I'll add server-side acceptance to tolerate both while we roll. also will add an endpoint-level contract test that runs on merge to catch this class of mismatch.
Sam: cool. can you drop PR number here once open? I'll ping for code review. :thumbsup:
Anjali: will do — opening PR now. expecting id #2345. tagging @Mike for review.
Mike: got it, will review later today.
Sam: thanks all. following up in this thread after PR merge.
QA Bot: note: please bump e2e test matrix to include both `stop: null` and `stop: []` cases.
Anjali: added to checklist.
Sam: closing loop — created a tiny docs blurb to explain omission vs explicit stop behavior for SDKs, will add to changelog once PR merges.
Mike: thanks, that should help support tickets.
